claims.statement: Governor Newsom signed seven named data-centre bills on September 21, 2026.
claims.limits: The announcement identifies the package but cannot establish every law’s operative scope.

claims.statement: SB 1168 requires the Public Utilities Commission, in a new or existing proceeding, to assess opportunities for rate structures addressing data-centre transmission, distribution, load and procurement costs and residential cost pressures.
claims.limits: Assessment is not an adopted tariff or guaranteed household saving.

claims.statement: Neither the signing announcement nor SB 1168 establishes an immediate or quantified reduction in a household electricity bill.
claims.limits: A future commission proceeding could produce a rate structure; this packet has no adopted rate, utility case or bill calculation.

claims.statement: AB 1577 requires specified estimates when an owner or operator applies for a discretionary local permit, entitlement or land-use authorization for a covered data centre.
claims.limits: It applies at the specified application stage and only to covered facilities.

claims.statement: AB 1577 directs the Energy Commission to establish reporting after energization and at least annually, publish submitted information annually in anonymized aggregate form, and begin its data-centre load-trend assessment with the 2029 integrated energy policy report.
claims.limits: The commission sets submission manner and timing; facility-level energy data is not promised as a public dataset.

claims.statement: AB 1577 excludes facilities below 10 megawatts and named public, safety, national-security and utility facilities from the covered reporting provisions.
claims.limits: Use the exact statutory categories; do not generalize the exclusions to the other six laws.

claims.statement: This packet cannot yet describe the operative effect of AB 2383, AB 2469, AB 2619, SB 886 or SB 887.
claims.limits: The signing-page summaries and bill titles are insufficient for a comprehensive seven-law explainer.
